thread:
nina: FYI during today's nightly base-image rebuild a handful of canaries failed image-attest because cosign couldn't reach KMS. We also got a vuln alert for libssl from one of the legacy layers. Need quick coord: RBAC + audit export + vuln triage.
adai: which KMS error?
leo: saw this in the runner logs: `rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = Permission "cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign" denied for serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
vuln-scan-bot: scan 2026-04-02T02:12Z — gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-04-02 found CVE-2024-9999 (libssl). Details: https://vuln.redwood/CVE-2024-9999
infra: we rolled a project-level IAM change last night to tighten actAs and remove broad roles. That probably impacted the CI runner's ability to impersonate the signer SA.
sec-oncall: ok, treat unsigned-attest as P2 until re-signing plan in place. Also we must not change RBAC before ensuring KMS audit logs are exported to the secure-audit bucket.
nina: agreed. Emergency steps: (A) re-enable minimal actAs for CI runner for 60m so we can finish the canary queue and re-run attest/sign; (B) follow up with a least-priv rollout: per-cluster Workload Identity + KMS-only principal, with IAM Conditions restricting signing to named service accounts + timeframe.
adai: for (A) I can apply a temporary binding:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding signer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com \\
  --member=group:ci-runners@redwood.com --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountUser \\
  --condition=None
```
I'll annotate the change and set a 1hr timer.
leo: do we have audit export configured? If not we should enable logSink now so every KMS.access was captured before we flip stuff.
infra: audit-sink exists but a couple of projects (staging) didn't have the sink attached due to org-policy constraints. I'll attach sink to staging and verify export path.
sec-oncall: add an alert on the audit-pipeline: query for `protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricSign" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:signer@redwood*` and set to page after 3 failures in 15m.
nina: good. Also on the vuln side: libssl came from an old busybox-based layer we pulled in during rebase. We should patch/squash that layer and re-generate SBOMs.
adai: SBOMs are flaky because tar ordering and file mtimes differ after unpack -> repack. I propose we normalize by zeroing mtime and sorting entries in the SBOM generator:
```
find . -print0 | sort -z | tar --mtime='1970-01-01' -cf - --null -T - | sha256sum
```
That'll make SBOMs deterministic for identical content.
leo: nice. For the KMS/RBAC redesign we should use per-key IAM + IAM Conditions limiting `request.time` window and `resource.name` pattern. Plan: create terraform module `kms-signer-wid` that does WI binding and minimal roles.
infra: I'll open the module PR. It will include an automated smoke test that runs `cosign verify` and `cosign sign` against an ephemeral local test key mapped to the WI.
vuln-scan-bot: note: images that failed attest: gcr.io/redwood/service-a:canary-2026-04-02, gcr.io/redwood/worker:canary-2026-04-02
sec-oncall: we need owner notification for those services + schedule re-sign window. If we rotate the signer key, old images need re-attestation. Coordinate with product owners before mass re-sign.
nina: okay owners: @infra and @leo will coordinate re-sign schedule. Who wants the rollout doc? I can draft the steps and checklist.
adai: assign me terraform tasks and a rollout playbook entry for rollback semantics.
leo: I'll handle the SBOM normalization PR and a small tool to diff attestations ignoring non-deterministic meta.
infra: temporary IAM grant applied 2026-04-02T03:05Z, window 60m. Link to audit change: https://iam.redwood/audit/changes/78910
deploy-bot: re-run rebuild job triggered 2026-04-02T03:06Z — build 45287
leo: re-run succeeded and cosign signatures present. KMS logs show `AsymmetricSign` entries for signer@redwood.
sec-oncall: confirm audit export reachability and create the alert. Also add a runbook step: "before any key rotation or RBAC hardening, ensure sink attached and retention policy documented."
nina: I'll file GH issues: #k8s-wid-signer, #sbom-determinism, #signer-key-rotation. Assignments: nina -> rollout doc, adaI -> terraform WI module, leo -> SBOM + compare tool, infra -> audit sink + sign schedule.
infra: PRs incoming. ETA for full WI rollout: 2 weeks if no blockers.
sec-oncall: we will reconvene in 24h to verify audit retention and that the signer key rotation plan includes owner-signoff and re-sign window.
leo: one small follow-up: add selinux label normalization to the SBOM step too (we have seen labels differ across kernel builds).
nina: added. Thanks all. If anything else fails re-open here or ping #incidents. :white_check_mark:
